Entry trigger: An enters-the-battlefield condition appears in a trigger. It can refer to this card or to another permanent entering.
Death / leave trigger: The trigger names dying or leaving the battlefield. Death requires a creature to go from the battlefield to a graveyard; other leave triggers can work on exile.
Attack trigger: The event is declaring an attack. Unlike combat damage, this does not require an attacker to connect.
Combat damage trigger: The event requires dealing combat damage. Check whether the recipient must be a player.
Cast trigger: The event is casting a spell. Simply putting a permanent onto the battlefield is not casting it.
Upkeep / end-step trigger: A trigger is tied to a particular upkeep or end step; it is not immediately available on deployment.
Sacrifice to activate: Sacrificing a permanent is part of an activation cost. The paid resource is gone before opponents can respond to the ability.
Instant / flash face: An instant face, flash, or explicit permission to cast this card as though it had flash. Other modes and faces may have different timing.
Sorcery face: At least one face is a sorcery; permissions and alternative faces may change what is available.
Permanent setup: The library face is a nonland permanent. Activated and triggered effects may need that permanent to resolve and remain in play.
Land play: A front-face land. Playing a land is not casting a spell; mana and nonmana abilities have their own requirements.
Activated ability: Printed cost-and-effect wording with a colon, including mana and loyalty abilities; not an assertion of immediate usability.
Triggered ability: Printed when, whenever, or beginning/end-of-event wording. Check the trigger and any intervening condition.
Loyalty ability: Planeswalker with an activated ability. Starting loyalty, sorcery timing and loyalty costs matter.
Ability from hand: The card has a hand ability such as cycling or channel. The activation is not casting its spell face.
Restricted timing: Printed once-per-turn, sorcery-only, or other explicit timing restriction. Read the affected clause.
Instant / flash spell: At least one castable face is an instant or has flash. Not the timing of every face, nor a guarantee of available mana.
Own alternate payment: Explicit alternate cost, self-discount, evoke, foretell, suspend, prototype, affinity or similar. Can still require setup, payment or delayed access.
Deploy other cards: Moves other cards into play by an alternative route, including reanimation. Not all routes are free. Includes commander routes and high-gate abilities.
Spell discounts: Reduces other spell costs, distinct from producing mana and from activated-ability discounts.
Ability discounts: Reduces or replaces an activated/equip cost, not spell costs.
Hand ability: Channel, cycling or ninjutsu options; not spells cast for their printed face cost.
Destroy: Destruction coverage; generally stopped by indestructible. Costs, targeting and restrictions still apply.
Exile / sacrifice: Battlefield exile or forced sacrifice/exile choices. Conditional until-leaves exile is included; not every case is permanent or targeted.
Bounce / tuck: Returns opposing resources to hand/library; usually temporary denial rather than card elimination.
Damage / shrink: Damage, fight or negative toughness can remove creatures of suitable size; not an unconditional kill.
Tap / disable: Tap, prevent untapping, or disable attacks/abilities. Some cards prevent untapping without doing the tapping.
Temporary exile / phase: Short-term exile/return or phasing, not permanent removal.
Steal / transform: Change control or neutralize abilities/types. Does not inherently remove the card.
Counter / stack: Interact with spells or abilities already on the stack; includes noncounter answers with different restrictions.
Multi-permanent reset: Can remove multiple battlefield permanents with a sweep/overload/mode. May be conditional or symmetric; not necessarily a complete wipe.
Taxes / restrictions: Restrict casting, activation, untapping, drawing or combat, or impose resource taxes. Does not mean a complete lock.
Protect board: Protect other owned permanents via a printed protective effect. Not an exhaustive count of defensive keywords on individual threats.
Graveyard disruption: Direct graveyard removal, replacement, or access restriction. Scope ranges from one card to whole graveyards.
Enable targeting / damage: Remove hexproof/shroud/indestructible as specified by the card; requires another effect to answer the permanent.
Combat prevention / redirection: Prevent combat damage, stop attacks, or redirect attackers. Not permanent removal or a general combo answer.
Hand disruption: Can cause an opposing player to discard or exile a hand card; includes conditional, symmetrical and choice-based modes. Self-only filtering is excluded.
Recover other cards: Can return/recast other used cards, including narrow targets, death triggers and high-gate ultimates. Graveyard access can be disrupted.
Own-card reuse: Can a card can reuse itself. Usually conditional or finite, not necessarily an engine by itself.
Blink / return: Reuse a surviving permanent through exile/return. Usually does not recover a lost permanent; tokens do not return.
Copy / imprint: Copy a permanent/spell/ability or replay an imprinted copy. Needs a valid source; not automatically a replacement for a destroyed engine.
Untap support: Can untap resources. Can enable repeated nonmana abilities as well as mana production; may be gated.
Recurring draw: Repeated opportunities to draw. Trigger costs, caps and dependencies still apply; counts are not cards drawn per turn.
Entry draw: A draw-on-entry permanent. Can become recurring if this deck can reuse it; does not itself imply a repeatable loop.
Token production: Can create tokens for you, including creature, mana and other artifact tokens. Pure replacements/multipliers and gift-token removal are excluded. Setup and ultimate gates still apply.
Token modifiers: Changes or multiplies a token-creation event without being a token source on its own.
Return own to hand: Can retrieve a surviving owned permanent to recast, or return itself to hand. Not graveyard recovery and not a free replay.
Creatures: A mode can affect an opposing creature.
Artifacts: A mode can affect an opposing artifact.
Enchantments: A mode can affect an opposing enchantment.
Planeswalkers: A mode can affect an opposing planeswalker.
Lands: A mode can affect an opposing land; restricted targets count.
Graveyards: Can disrupt access to a graveyard, including a single card.
Hands: Can reduce or constrain an opposing hand.
Stack spells: Can answer a spell before it resolves.
Stack abilities: Can answer an activated or triggered ability on the stack.
Repeatable mana rock: Noncreature, nonland artifact with a printed mana ability that does not sacrifice itself. Includes filtering rocks and conditional activations.
Mana creature: Nonland creature with a printed repeatable add-mana activation. Does not count every way to grant another creature a mana ability.
One-shot mana: A spell that adds mana directly or a nonland permanent that sacrifices itself for mana. Treasure producers are not automatically fast mana.
Land search to hand: Search for a land or named basic land type and put it into hand, including landcycling. This helps land drops but does not itself put an extra land onto the battlefield.
Land search to field: Library land search that puts a land onto the battlefield; includes fetch lands and tapped arrivals. Not all are net acceleration.
Fetch land: Land sacrificed to search the library for a land to put onto the battlefield.
Grant flash to others: A printed effect lets other cards or spells be cast with flash timing. Count separately from a card having flash itself.
Interaction-capable: Distinct cards with any tagged interaction target or method. The union, not the sum of columns.
Instant / flash interaction: Interaction-capable cards with an instant or flash face. Not every mode of every face works at instant speed.
Permanent-based interaction: Interaction-capable cards with a permanent type other than land. May require resolution, another cost or a later trigger.
Hand ability interaction: Interaction-capable cards also tagged with an ability from hand. Check the card: the interactive mode need not be that same ability.
